summary: Elevated 5xx + long tail latency from third-party webhook retry storm and healthcheck oscillation
description:
Issue summary: Multiple customers (largest impact: Verse Labs) observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses from the Redwood API gateway beginning ~2026-03-13 22:10 UTC and continuing in waves through the night. Impact: Increased 502/503/504 rates for embedding and streaming routes, long tail latencies (p99 > 12s), some streaming sessions dropped. Environment: prod us-east region, dedicated cluster for Verse Labs.

Observed behavior:
- API gateway returned 502/503 for a subset of routes; error-rate spike correlated with high retry volume from external webhook callbacks originating from Verse Labs' integration.
- Upstream runtimes experienced GC pauses and NVMe iowait spikes during the same windows; multiple runtimes were momentarily marked unhealthy by the ingress healthcheck and cycle-removed then re-added (healthcheck thrash).
- KV-prefetch lock contention increased on embedding shard 7 leading to slower cold starts for model shards and higher FBT.

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) Large batch embedding upload + webhook fanout from Verse Labs triggers external retries (their webhook provider replays).
2) Apigw accept queue and ephemeral port pressure rises, connection churn increases.
3) Healthcheck latency increases for runtimes; ingress marks instances unhealthy and triggers churn.
4) Runtimes hit GC and NVMe background compaction during spike; prefetched KV misses and iowait slow down model init -> increased FBT and 5xx cascade.

Immediate logs & metrics (excerpts):
- apigw metrics (22:12 UTC): accept_queue_depth=487 (+320 baseline), ephemeral_ports_free=12 -> 502 rate +1400% vs baseline
- runtime node nvr-07: nvme_iowait=78%, gc_pause_ms=1563, healthcheck_latency_ms=810 -> marked Unhealthy at 22:13:04
- embedding shard 7: prefetch_lock_wait_count=2400, avg_wait_ms=42 -> first_byte_time 1.2s -> 11.9s

Customer impact: high for Verse Labs (timeouts affecting embedding ingestion and streaming), multiple customer calls escalated to support.

Attachments: log snippets, Grafana dashboard links, Slack thread #support-verse (link in comments).
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a burst of webhook retries from a single tenant while performing large embedding uploads
Observe accept_queue growth and ephemeral port exhaustion on apigw
Watch runtime healthcheck latency and NVMe iowait increase until runtimes are cycled
comments: 2026-03-13 22:25 UTC - Aisha Kapoor: Customer reported elevated 502s during large embedding upload + webhook callback fanout. Attached customer cURL trace and timestamps.

2026-03-13 22:45 UTC - Miguel Santos (SRE): Initial triage: apigw accept queue and ephemeral port exhaustion seen; correlates with repeated webhook retries from Verse Labs inbound IPs. Forwarding to runtime team to inspect NVMe/gc metrics.

2026-03-13 23:10 UTC - Priya Nair (runtime): Observed long GC pauses on 3 nodes and NVMe compaction I/O spikes around the same windows. Suspect background snapshot compaction running concurrently with heavy prefetch workload.

2026-03-14 01:02 UTC - Support (Aisha): Applied temporary rate limit on the /webhook callback route for Verse Labs at edge (limit: 30 req/s) and enabled route-level circuit breaker; customer reports fall in immediate 502s.
2026-03-14 03:15 UTC - Miguel Santos: Deployed hotfix to apigw that increases accept_queue_size threshold and tunes ephemeral port reuse for high-churn tenants. Monitoring for regression.
2026-03-14 09:05 UTC - Runbook owner (Olga Petrov): Scheduled NVMe compaction jobs to off-peak windows and added prefetch backoff during high-load. Follow-up RFC created.

2026-03-14 11:20 UTC - Customer (Verse Labs): Confirmed reduced errors after rate-limiting and hotfix; still seeing occasional long-tail p99 on embeddings during large imports (investigating client-side batching).
investigation_notes: Correlated apigw accept_queue spikes with increased connection churn from a small set of customer IPs (webhook provider replaying callbacks).
Healthcheck oscillation: ingress healthcheck latency crossed threshold due to slow response from runtimes (GC + NVMe iowait). This caused mass endpoint churn and cascade.
KV-prefetch hotspots: embedding shard 7 experienced lock contention when many cold-prefetches occurred concurrently, compounding model init time.
Reproduced locally with synthetic replay: high-churn TCP connections + background NVMe compaction -> increased gc pauses and failed healthchecks.
resolution:
Mitigations applied: (1) temporary route-level rate limit and circuit breaker for Verse Labs' webhook route; (2) apigw hotfix to raise accept_queue thresholds and adjust ephemeral port reuse to reduce 502s during churn; (3) rescheduled NVMe compaction/background snapshot tasks to off-peak; (4) implemented prefetch backoff heuristic in serving runtime to reduce lock contention under heavy cold-prefetch.

Follow-up plan: create permanent tenant-level webhook ingestion throttling feature, add telemetry for webhook-origin churn, build automatic healthcheck hysteresis to avoid oscillation, and add prewarm suggestions to console for large embedding uploads. Owner: Miguel Santos. ETA for full rollout: 2026-03-21.
next_steps: Finalize postmortem and circulate to SRE/Product/Dev teams
Implement tenant webhook throttling RFC and begin design work
Add telemetry for prefetch lock wait and webhook-origin connection churn to per-tenant dashboards
